messages:
alan: Kicking off a staged rollout of 'burstline-microhold' to prod GPU pools. Quick wins from canary: p50 -14%, p99 -28%, token cost -10% on conversational traces. Rolling slowly. :rocket:

infra-bot: canary results (canary-9 -> prod): p50 100ms -> 86ms (-14%), p99 500ms -> 360ms (-28%), token cost $0.0095 -> $0.0086 (-10%), errors steady.

rachel: what changed exactly? scheduler, prefetch, both?

alan: small combo: predictive micro-hold (up to 8ms) in microbatcher + an ephemeral hot-prefix shadow to avoid remote KV hops for short-tail requests. No model changes.

jason: rollback/kill-switch? need it in runbook.

alan: feature-flag `runtime.burstline_microhold` per-pool. Rollback: `POST /release/flags/runtime.burstline_microhold/disable` body `{"pool":"<pool>"}`. Runbook updated: https://go/redwood/runbooks/burstline-microhold

ops: adding canary check for owners:
```
# compare p99 per pool between canary and prod
python infra/compare.py --metric p99_latency --from canary-9 --to prod --group pool
```

deploy-bot: feature `runtime.burstline_microhold` enabled on gpu-us-west-2a, gpu-eu-west-1a; continuing rollout in 25m.

alan: thanks team  big props to microbatch + kv-prefetch folks, will post brief graphs after full rollout.
